title: A Yearbook for the Semester
premise: Mirabel Brightwater has spent three years at Ashgrove Academy keeping her head down, counting the days until graduation frees her from a school that treats scholarship kids like ghosts. When her college essay prompt demands she write about 'a community that shaped you,' she can't answer honestly without admitting the academy's yearbook archives have been quietly scrubbed—names of expelled students, including her missing friend Odette, erased from every record. As Mirabel and a ragtag group of misfits dig into what the school board buried, they uncover a pattern of quiet expulsions designed to protect donors' children. The climax forces Mirabel to choose between a full-ride recommendation from the headmaster and publishing the truth; she chooses truth, and the novel ends at graduation, where the students publish their own unauthorized yearbook—one that finally says everyone's name.
about_author: Jude Crane is the pen name of a former boarding school scholarship student who spent years convinced they were forgettable. They now write stories about the kids in the margins of other people's photographs.

chapters.title: The Counting Habit
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Opening on day 214 of her countdown to graduation, we see Ashgrove through her practiced invisibility: perfect grades, no friends, no footprint. A glimpse of the empty chair where her friend Odette used to sit establishes the wound beneath the routine. Emotional beat: numbness as armor.

chapters.title: One Honest Question
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. English teacher Mr. Okafor assigns the college essay: 'Describe a community that shaped you.' Mirabel stares at a blank page for hours, realizing she has curated herself out of every community she's been part of. Emotional beat: the first crack in her armor—she wants an answer she doesn't have.

chapters.title: The Yearbook Room
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Sent to fetch archival photos for the school's anniversary display, Mirabel discovers the yearbook vault—and notices Odette's name has been razor-bladed out of every volume. Her hands shake. Emotional beat: cold dread replacing apathy; the countdown suddenly feels like a cover-up's timeline.

chapters.title: People Who Notice
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Theo Vasquez, yearbook editor and chronic overachiever, catches Mirabel photographing the defaced pages. Instead of reporting her, he admits he's noticed gaps too—his brother was 'transferred' two years ago. Emotional beat: wary alliance; being seen feels dangerous and necessary.

chapters.title: Rules of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Flashback chapter to freshman-year Odette, who taught Mirabel how scholarship kids survive Ashgrove: never draw attention, never owe anyone anything. Present-day Mirabel realizes Odette broke her own rules right before disappearing. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into guilt.

chapters.title: The Scholarship Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The pair sneaks into the bursar's office and finds a ledger showing scholarship enrollments dropping sharply each spring—always after a donor incident. Mirabel recognizes three names as 'transfers' she'd been told about. Emotional beat: horror of pattern recognition; this is systemic.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Margins
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. To widen the search, they recruit the invisible kids: Priya, who runs the lost-and-found and remembers everything; Dez, a groundskeeper's son who knows the buildings' bones; and quiet June, whose sister was expelled. Emotional beat: tentative found-family forming around shared erasure.

chapters.title: What June Remembers
chapters.summary: June's POV. June reveals her sister Lena received a settlement offer contingent on silence—a signed NDA in exchange for tuition elsewhere. She kept the envelope. Emotional beat: fear turning to fury; the buried thing has a paper trail.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Gala
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the school's centennial gala, Mirabel serves canapés on scholarship duty while watching the board members toast 'tradition.' Headmaster Voss singles her out warmly—the best students get mentored, he says. Emotional beat: seduction of belonging offered by the enemy.

chapters.title: An Offer With Teeth
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Voss offers Mirabel a funded summer research program and his personal recommendation letter—if she drops her 'distractions.' He never names them, which tells her everything. Emotional beat: temptation crystallized; invisibility was always a transaction.

chapters.title: Odette's Locker
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following a hunch from the ledger dates, they open the long-sealed locker 114 and find Odette's journal: she'd discovered a donor's son falsified records that got a scholarship student expelled, and she planned to go to the board. Emotional beat: heartbreak and resolve; Odette wasn't transferred—she was silenced.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group fights about risk: publication could tank all their futures, especially the seniors needing recommendations. Theo accuses Mirabel of using the cause to avoid writing her essay; Mirabel walks out. Emotional beat: found family tested by fear; the cost becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Essay That Won't Lie
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Alone, Mirabel finally writes her college essay—not about Ashgrove's prestige, but about the yearbook room and the people willing to look. Reading it back, she understands what she's actually choosing. Emotional beat: clarity; the question nobody can stop answering has answered her.

chapters.title: Reconciliation in the Archive
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez finds Mirabel asleep in the archive and coaxes the group back together with a plan: instead of one leak, they'll build a complete counter-record—every erased name, date, and document—hidden inside a legitimate project. Emotional beat: repair; the family chooses each other again.

chapters.title: The Counter-Yearbook
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Working nights, they compile 'A Yearbook for the Semester': photos, testimonies, the ledger scans, Odette's journal pages. Priya's memory fills gaps; June's NDA envelope provides the smoking gun. Emotional beat: purpose; grief converted into craft.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Someone tips off Voss. He searches dorms, suspends Theo pending 'honor review,' and calls Mirabel in—not to threaten her, but to show her Odette's file and imply Odette chose to leave. Emotional beat: darkest hour; the machinery of erasure turns on them personally.

chapters.title: Choosing Sides Out Loud
chapters.summary: June's POV. June does the bravest small thing: she mails copies of the NDA envelope to three board members known to dislike Voss, then tells the group. The adults are no longer a monolith. Emotional beat: hope rekindled by an ordinary act of courage.

chapters.title: The Board Hearing
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Summoned before the board, Mirabel abandons the safe statement Mr. Okafor helped her draft and reads Odette's journal aloud instead, naming every erased student. A dissenting board member, Mrs. Adeyemi, backs her with the mailed documents. Emotional beat: climax; visibility as defiance, voice as weapon.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unscripted
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Voss resigns under board pressure; Theo's suspension is reversed; an independent review of expulsions begins. But there's no cinematic victory—just paperwork, rumors, and the strange lightness of not hiding. Emotional beat: exhale; justice as process, not fireworks.

chapters.title: What Odette Would Say
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel visits Odette's family, returns the journal, and learns Odette is thriving at a state school—alive, unburied, reachable. They talk for three hours. Emotional beat: restoration; the missing friend was never gone, only made absent.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At commencement, the five of them distribute the counter-yearbook to every graduating senior—every name restored, including theirs. Voss's replacement shakes Mirabel's hand; she lets it mean nothing. Emotional beat: triumph of witness over erasure.

chapters.title: Day Zero
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, closing. On campus for one last night, Mirabel crosses out the final number on her countdown and writes her college essay's true last line: the community that shaped her built itself out of everyone the school tried to forget. She stops counting. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, memory kept, future open.
